Infinite Range Switch Desmystified Right Here! - Works perfect as a replacement to a similar looking stove switch on my smooth top stove. I didn't need one of the connections. Basically if your current switch has H1, H2, L1, L2, P, connections and the wattage reads 2100-2600w or 8.9-11.0A (amps) then this is the one for you. I had the large burner and there was a LOW connection (L1 I think) that I did not need to hook to. I suspect you may be able to use the same switch for a small burner and would likely not use one the of the HIGH connections. BUT if you have the large burner DON'T buy one that says 1250-1560W (watts) or 4.4-7.4A (amps). That is lower power than you will need. When hooking up the new one don't worry about the wire color, order or location since they vary in front vs. rear burner and brand to brand. Just copy the wire locations of your old switch to the new one: H1 to H1, L1 to L1, P to P, etc.. the spade locations and look of the switch were a bit different from stock but it works perfect and temperature is the same as the other large burner I measured with my digital thermometer. It is also possible the screw threads that hold it to the metal panel could also vary from what you have and it does not come with screws, I don't think any others do either. I lost my original switch screws anyway and I have a large screw jar so this was no biggie for me. If you need to replace the screws just use ones barely long enough to grab the front of the switch and not go deep in or you may ruin the switch or touch a contact. I hope this helps someone. I was overly worried about wire colors and switch shape, etc. It's ALL about wattage, connections (H1, L1) and the shaft that your knob slides onto. Match those and your good. FORGET brand loyalty. Frigidaire, Kenmore, Hotpoint, GE, Whirlpool, Amana, Electrolux, etc are all in bed together. Chances are your $2,000 GE 6 burner Profile stove has the same switch as the $449 Whirlpool apartment grade one.

My thinking on a fridge filter for lead: - The main difference between this filter and the OEM and more expensive replacements is that this does not filter out heavy metals like lead. My thinking is that if there is lead in my water supply then that is a much bigger problem than a fridge filter can fix! I only use the fridge water for drinking water, and if I am using a small glass. If I am taking a big cup outside, drinking from my bathroom cup after brushing my teeth, or when I am cooking I use tap water, so if there was lead in my water supply this would hardly keep my family safe.

We have very high quality public water here in Phoenix, they test and report often. So unless I want to use water from the fridge filter for everything then a lead filter is, in my opinion, not neccessary.

My $0.02 and probably just about worth each penny!

Made in China. Know what you're getting, and you'll be fine. - It’s very important that you know exactly what you are getting with this machine. The pictures are a little deceiving. The top picture shows the icemaker chock full of ice. That is not how this machine works. You really need to watch the video to see how it works. There is a basket in the front where the ice is dropped and stored. When the small basket is full, the machine will stop producing ice. I have a 32 ounce water bottle and the basket will feel my water bottle with ice about two thirds full. The basket area is not cold like a freezer. So the ice will continue to melt… With the water flowing down into the water reservoir area… And more ice will be made. The only way you can continually make and save nice is if you remove the basket, about once per hour, and place the ice into a receptacle and place it in your freezer.

The listing shows that this icemaker will make 26 pounds of ice and 24 hours. Well, that’s only if you continually add water and continually remove the basket of ice and place the ice in your freezer. So unless you can do that every hour… Day and night… You are not going to end up with 26 pounds of ice.

I like this icemaker for what it is. And as long as you understand how it works, and don’t have extraordinarily high expectations, then you too may like this icemaker.
